transfers.label: Internet egress (out)
transfers.sub: data sent to the public internet
transfers.desc: Data leaving the cloud for the public internet — the headline cost line, and the charge that dominates most cloud networking bills.

aws.headline: $0.09 /GB
aws.note: First 100 GB each month is free, aggregated across AWS services and regions. Beyond that the rate steps down with volume as shown; transfers above 500 TB/month are contact-sales. Inbound data transfer from the internet is free.

azure.headline: $0.087 /GB
azure.note: Zone 1 rate — North America and Europe — over Microsoft's global network. The first 100 GB each month is free and inbound transfer is free. A Routing Preference of Internet routing prices a little lower.

gcp.headline: $0.12 /GiB
gcp.note: Premium network tier, to worldwide destinations other than China and Australia. The Standard tier is cheaper — roughly $0.085 then $0.065 per GiB from a US region — and carries a 200 GB monthly free allowance per region. Google bills per GiB, slightly larger than a GB.

transfers.label: Cross-AZ, same region
transfers.desc: Data moving between Availability Zones inside one region — the running cost of a multi-AZ, highly-available architecture.

aws.headline: $0.01 /GB
aws.note: Charged at one cent per GB on both the sending and the receiving side, so a round trip between Availability Zones effectively costs about two cents per GB. Applies to private-IP traffic across AZs.

azure.headline: Free
azure.note: Azure no longer charges for data transfer between Availability Zones in the same region — inter-AZ billing was formally eliminated, announced during 2024. The raw retail-price API still exposes legacy one-cent meters that are not billed.

gcp.headline: $0.01 /GiB
gcp.note: One cent per GiB for VM-to-VM traffic between zones of the same region, billed on the sending side. Traffic inside a single zone over internal IPs is free.

transfers.label: Cross-region, same cloud
transfers.desc: Data transfer from one of the provider's regions to another — replication, multi-region failover and cross-region backups.

aws.headline: $0.02 /GB
aws.note: Representative rate between two US regions, billed on egress from the source region with inbound free. Between the two US-East regions — N. Virginia and Ohio — it is one cent per GB. The exact rate depends on the source region, so non-US origins differ.

azure.headline: $0.02 /GB
azure.note: Standard inter-region transfer, North America to North America, billed on egress from the source region with inbound free. The rate varies by source continent.

gcp.headline: $0.01 /GiB
gcp.note: US or Canada region to US or Canada region, under Google Cloud's current Data Transfer pricing model, billed on the sending side. Some third-party sources cite two cents — that figure usually refers to Cloud Storage cross-region replication, a separate charge. Cross-continent transfer costs more; confirm your exact region pair on the linked page.

transfers.label: NAT gateway data processing
transfers.desc: The per-gigabyte surcharge for traffic routed through a managed NAT gateway — separate from, and on top of, the gateway's hourly charge.

aws.headline: $0.045 /GB
aws.note: Per-GB data-processing charge for every gigabyte through a NAT gateway, to any destination. It is on top of the separate NAT gateway hourly charge of about 4.5 cents, and on top of internet-egress charges.

azure.headline: $0.045 /GB
azure.note: Data processed through an Azure NAT Gateway, inbound and outbound. Separate from the NAT gateway hourly resource charge of about 4.5 cents per hour.

gcp.headline: $0.045 /GiB
gcp.note: Data processed through Cloud NAT, both ingress and egress. Separate from the small hourly Cloud NAT charge billed per VM.

transfers.label: Private interconnect (egress)
transfers.desc: Outbound data over a dedicated private link — AWS Direct Connect, Azure ExpressRoute or Google Cloud Interconnect — the route to your own datacentre or another cloud that sidesteps full internet-egress rates.

aws.headline: $0.02 /GB
aws.note: AWS Direct Connect data-transfer-out, from a US region to a US Direct Connect location — a flat rate with no tiers. Port-hour fees are billed separately.

azure.headline: $0.025 /GB
azure.note: Azure ExpressRoute outbound on the Metered plan, Zone 1. Inbound is free; the Unlimited plan replaces metering with a higher fixed port fee.

gcp.headline: $0.02 /GiB
gcp.note: Google Cloud Interconnect — Dedicated or Partner — outbound, US to US. Inbound is not charged; VLAN-attachment and port fees are separate.
